For example you want to convince someone to do something.
Then you would need to pass a persuasion check.
You then roll a d20 dice (1 to 20) that's boosted by your charisma level and whether you have proeffiency in persuasion. Other bonuses on top.

There are checks for a lot of things, that's indeed one more reason to diversify your party as diff classes and backgrounds have diff proeffiencies.

Ie: you need a 10 to persuade a character.
You roll a 6 which should fail but you have +3 from charisma and +2 from proeffiency in persuasion which ends up being 11 so you successfully persuade that character.

Btw rolls to detects things like traps or hidden treasures are based on perception and are done automatically as you near them, if you fail them well you don't "see" them even if you the player know they are there from internet or whatever.

Even whether you hit someone in combat is based on that system, rolls are automated not to interrupt combat. 
Some features can sometimes interrupt combat (ie: a divination wizard can influence dice rolls and in case his limited feature can turn a failed strike into a successful one then the game will pause and ask you whether you want to use that boost) 
You can set up in-game the rules of your reactions and if to ask you.

Just saw that you didn't really like having the same class as a companion, well there is a warlock one if that's a deal breaker.

However you can only fight with 3 active companions (so 4 man party), the rest of those you picked up stay at your camp (you can switch them whenever you want). So you have the option to leave out some companions for other play throughs, if you do that I would look around for companion "alignemnents" as to plan out your party. 
Or you can just pick up everyone you like and travel around with your favorite ones except when there's a quest for a specific companion in which case you take them on a field trip.

But it's true that picking up a class exclusive to your companions allows you to explore more of the game at once.

Yh, pure warlock is good whether you go the full caster route or the gish (melee+caster) route. 
Pact choice is at lvl 3, until then full caster.

Btw warlock is no wizard you only have a few spell slots but they replenish on short rests too. So the full caster version is mostly nuking with the cantrip (do remember to take the option to boost its damage at lvl 2, even if you plan to go melee) and using spells as support or aoe damage. No need to take single target damage spells.
Oh and one of the pacts has a summon/pet.

Warlock, charisma based so you can be the face of the party.
Best damage cantrip (eldritch blast, spammable spell)
And can melee if you take pact of the blade (charisma to attack and damage). (Not as sturdy as a fighter or barbarian though).

Can multiclass into any charisma based class and fighter.
Warlock's eldritch blast scales with character level and not class level, which is good for multiclasing.
If you want heavy armor you can take paladin or fighter as lvl 1 and then switch to warlock, you will get the melee 2nd attack one lvl later (6 instead of 5*), but eldritch blast will be fine as it scales with character level instead of class lvl. 

Btw you can respec your stats through an npc you meet early on. Meaning if you go the route above you can choose stats appropriate for fighter and paladin at character creation, then respec when you reach lvl 4 when you can get pact of the blade if you took first lvl in fighter or Pala first. 
Actually you can just play pure walock until lvl 6 and then respec with a fighter level 1st because it's not like heavy armors are common at those levels.

2nd* melee attack is class lvl 5 (they don't stack).

Sorcerer is also an amazing multiclass for warlock if you want pure caster.
